\(27^{\cos 2x}\cdot 81^{\sin 2x}=3^{3\cos 2x}\cdot 3^{4\sin 2x}=3^{\,3\cos 2x+4\sin 2x}\).

The exponent \(3\cos 2x+4\sin 2x\) has amplitude \(\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5\), so it ranges over \([-5,5]\) and both endpoints are attained. The expression therefore ranges over \([3^{-5},\,3^{5}]\), and its minimum is \(3^{-5}=\dfrac{1}{243}\). Matches option A.

Source-verified against the printed NDA Maths practice Calculus booklet Q2526 and its answer key: the printed options are exactly (a) \([-1,\infty)\), (b) \((-\infty,-1)\), (c) \((-\infty,-1]\), (d) \((-1,\infty)\), and the printed key is (d). But \(f\) is strictly increasing on the CLOSED interval too — for \(-1\le x_1<x_2\) we have \(f(x_1)<f(x_2)\), e.g. \(f(-1)=-6<f(0)=-5\) — so option (a) is equally true and is in fact the maximal such interval. Strict monotonicity does not require \(f'>0\) at an isolated endpoint. The printed key (d) is retained here to match the source; a student answering (a) is not wrong.]

\(f(x)=x^{2}+2x-5\Rightarrow f'(x)=2x+2\), which is positive for \(x>-1\). Hence \(f\) is strictly increasing on \((-1,\infty)\), and equally on \([-1,\infty)\) since \(f'\) vanishes only at the single point \(x=-1\). Matches option D as printed.

The light is not green for \(5+30=35\) seconds of every \(60\)-second cycle, so the probability is \(\dfrac{35}{60}=\dfrac{7}{12}\). Matches option D.
